qualifiedQuestions: Index 6 (position 7): the note lists crabs, shrimp and lobster. Is English "the shellfish" meant as crustaceans only here, or as crustaceans and mollusks?
Index 6 (position 7): the note says to ask about both crustáceos and mariscos. Should a separate mariscos draft be added for this row?
Indexes 6 (7), 9 (10) and 16 (17): the Spanish source uses crustáceos at 6 and 16 but mariscos at 9. Is this shift intentional?
Index 9 (position 10): what does "mariscos" cover in the target regional usage? The Spanish-side draft marks the open extent with など only.
Index 9 (position 10): both drafts render "option"/"opción" as 料理. Is that the intended noun, or should it be a menu choice (メニュー, 選択肢)?
Index 16 (position 17): English says "any shellfish" and Spanish says "algún crustáceo". Should both drafts be kept, and which source governs if they are not reconciled?
Index 16 (position 17): is です/ます polite form with すみません the right level for a diner addressing a server, as the proposed equivalent of usted?
Within any broad label, should the groups (crustaceans, bivalves, cephalopods) be listed separately instead of implied to be equivalent?
No allergen scope, safe-to-eat status or labeling-category match is proposed, and no draft should be read as one. Should such a scope be defined separately, and by whom?
All dictionary entries are working glosses (reviewed: false). Which should a reviewer with English, Spanish and Japanese coverage check before use?

甲殻類 and 貝類 are not interchangeable: the alternatives expose the English/Spanish source conflict instead of treating either as the chosen allergen scope.
